sources.note: Extends a single-block interaction theorem to ablated subsets spanning many layers, isolates the cross-layer remainder as an exact double integral rather than bounding it, supplies the one missing closed-form ingredient (a local attention Jacobian bound, verified without a violation on a real 1.5B model), and tests the whole picture on an emergent circuit nobody designed for it — reporting the mixed outcome as mixed.
sources.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

sources.note: Treats a transformer forward pass as a controlled dynamical system with depth as time, lifts it with the Koopman operator to get a finite linear realisation whose spectrum is coordinate-free, proves that spectrum is recoverable from finite calibration data at the parametric rate, and then proves that the identifiable object and the human-legible object cannot be the same object.
sources.title: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability

sources.note: Points out that the group-relative policy gradient is a second-order U-statistic over pairs of rollouts rather than a sum of independent per-rollout contributions, and reallocates rollout compute accordingly -- treating prefixes as vertices and pair-gradient terms as edges, then correcting the resulting selection bias by inverse joint-inclusion weighting.
sources.title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR

sources.note: Measures, under a pre-registered confirmatory design, how often majority-vote self-consistency lowers per-problem accuracy on a hard science benchmark, and shows that two cheap verifier-free gates recover essentially none of the headroom a per-problem oracle marks out.
sources.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'pre-registration'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.

result.definition: Fixing hypotheses, thresholds and analysis choices before looking at the confirmatory data, and across 4 sources a practice rare enough in this literature that the archive records who does it. The fullest instance splits 198 problems into 47 exploratory and 151 confirmatory, locks four hypotheses and their thresholds at a git tag before any confirmatory analysis, sets each threshold on the permissive side of the exploratory estimate so it is a genuine prediction rather than a restatement, decides pass or fail on the confirmatory set only, and works out a one-sided boundary sensitivity showing its reported rate can only rise. Two theoretical sources in the set pre-register a test on a real pretrained model after deriving it, which is the same discipline applied to a prediction rather than to a hypothesis, and one of them withdraws its own empirical separation when it fails out of sample. A fourth pre-registers an allocation comparison. The archive's reading is that pre-registration is what converts a plausible margin into evidence in a field where most margins are single-run and uninterval-ed.
